## 1. Scope, evidence basis and reproduction

### What this analysis is

A descriptive profile of the verified NF-UNSW-NB15-v3 source population. It covers the
schema and column roles, the target distributions, raw data quality, the quantitative
feature distributions and the relationships between semantically compatible features.

### What this analysis is not

- It is not a model, a benchmark or an experiment result.
- It does not fit any transformer, selector, scaler, imputer or encoder.
- It does not select the final feature set and it does not choose a threshold or a
  hyperparameter.
- It does not remove, de-duplicate or re-label a single source row.

### Evidence classes used in this report

| Evidence class | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `EXECUTED ON REAL DATA` | Computed by this EDA run over every row of the verified file. |
| `SAMPLE-BASED` | Estimated from the seeded reservoir sample; size, method and seed are stated. |
| `INHERITED` | Reused from the verified quality report of PR #36 without re-computation. |
| `NOT VERIFIED` | No evidence exists yet; the claim is explicitly not made. |

Inherited duplicate and token findings are cross-checked against the values recomputed
by this run; the comparison result is recorded in section 8 and in the summary artifact.

### Reproduction order

```text
python scripts/check_environment.py
python scripts/fetch_nf_unsw_nb15_v3.py
python scripts/dataset_manifest.py verify
python scripts/validate_data.py
python scripts/eda_nf_unsw_nb15_v3.py
```

`scripts/validate_data.py` must run first: the EDA reuses its manifest contract and
byte verification instead of duplicating them. The EDA run itself re-verifies the source
SHA-256 against `data/NF_UNSW_NB15_V3_MANIFEST.json` before any analysis is executed.

Environment used for the recorded run: Python 3.14.6 on Windows 11, pandas 2.3.3, numpy 2.5.3.

against 127,693 attack flows, 94.6017% against

### Multiclass target `Attack`

| Attack category | Flows | Share |
|---|---|---|
| Benign | 2,237,731 | 94.6017% |
| Exploits | 42,748 | 1.8072% |
| Fuzzers | 33,816 | 1.4296% |
| Generic | 19,651 | 0.8308% |
| Reconnaissance | 17,074 | 0.7218% |
| DoS | 5,980 | 0.2528% |
| Backdoor | 4,659 | 0.1970% |
| Shellcode | 2,381 | 0.1007% |
| Analysis | 1,226 | 0.0518% |
| Worms | 158 | 0.0067% |

The three rarest categories are `Worms` (158 rows), `Analysis` (1,226 rows), `Shellcode` (2,381 rows). `Worms` is the rarest class in the dataset.

### Interpretation of the imbalance risk

- A default classifier that predicts the majority class already reaches
  94.6017% accuracy. Accuracy is therefore not a meaningful metric
  for this dataset; the evaluation plan has to report per-category recall and a
  macro-averaged score instead.
- The rare categories are far too small to support a stable per-class model on their
  own. `Worms` has 158 rows in total, so a single split that
  distributes it across partitions can leave one or two partitions without a single
  example.
- Stratification, resampling and threshold selection therefore have to be decided on
  the training partition only, and the decision has to be recorded with the split
  identifier. Choosing a strategy that looks at the full label distribution would leak
  test information.
- The rarest categories are also the categories most exposed to the duplicate findings
  in section 4, because deduplication strategies that keep the first occurrence change
  rare-class counts the most.

## 4. Data quality

### Missing, blank and non-finite tokens

Token classes are counted separately so that a blank cell, a literal `NaN`, a positive
infinity, a negative infinity and an invalid numeric token never collapse into one
number. The counters come from the streaming pass of
`scripts/validate_data.py` and from the token refinement pass of this EDA run.

| Column | blank | NaN | null | +Inf | -Inf | invalid |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SRC_TO_DST_SECOND_BYTES` | 63,425 | 0 | 0 | 59,068 | 0 | 0 |
| `DST_TO_SRC_SECOND_BYTES` | 0 | 0 | 0 | 122,493 | 0 | 0 |

Columns without any entry in this table contain only finite, non-negative values. No
row of the source file was modified, normalised or rewritten.

### Zero and near-zero flow durations

The two rate fields (`SRC_TO_DST_SECOND_BYTES`, `DST_TO_SRC_SECOND_BYTES`) carry the
non-finite values; the two average-throughput fields (`SRC_TO_DST_AVG_THROUGHPUT`,
`DST_TO_SRC_AVG_THROUGHPUT`) are finite on every row. The contingency table below
cross-tabulates the published duration with the non-finite rate and throughput state.

| duration_zero / rate_non_finite / throughput_non_finite | Flows |
|---|---|
| duration_zero=False, rate_non_finite=False, throughput_non_finite=False | 2,242,931 |
| duration_zero=True, rate_non_finite=True, throughput_non_finite=False | 122,493 |

122,493 flows have a zero published duration and a non-finite rate
value, while 0 flows have a zero duration and a finite rate
value. The non-finite rate values therefore occur **only** on zero-duration flows.

This is an **association observed in the published bytes**. The feature dictionary does
not expose the producer arithmetic, so this report does **not** claim that a division by
zero caused the infinities, and it does not treat the association as a causal relation.
The affected rows are kept, not dropped: the approved handling policy
(`docs/NF_UNSW_NB15_V3_PREPROCESSING_POLICY.md`) keeps zero-duration flows as a separate
observed condition and forbids replacing infinity with zero silently.

### Duplicate rows

| Fingerprint scope | Distinct rows | Repeated rows |
|---|---|---|
| Exact full row (55 columns) | 2,350,609 | 14,815 |
| Source feature (53 columns, targets excluded) | 2,350,609 | 14,815 |
| ML-feature equivalent (47 columns) | 1,230,871 | 1,134,553 |
| Behavioral-v1 (47 columns, separate namespace) | 1,230,871 | 1,134,553 |

Groups holding more than one row:

| Scope | Groups with duplicates |
|---|---|
| Exact full row | 14,815 |
| ML-feature equivalent | 189,788 |

Label conflicts inside repeated groups:

| Conflict | Groups | Rows |
|---|---|---|
| Binary `Label` conflict (0 and 1 in one group) | 0 | 0 |
| Multiple `Attack` categories in one group | 1,270 | 20,058 |
| `Benign` mixed with a malicious category | 0 | 0 |

The behavioral-v1 fingerprint uses the same ordered 47 columns as the ML baseline under a
separate namespace, so its equivalence classes and counts coincide with the
ML-feature-equivalent row by construction of the v3 contract.

### Why repeated rows must not be deleted automatically

1. **A repeat is not automatically a redundant copy.** NetFlow exporters emit one record
   per observed flow, and a legitimate network conversation can produce several records
   with an identical feature vector. Removing them would delete observed traffic, not
   duplicated bytes.
2. **Deletion is label-dependent.** The affected rows are not label-neutral: attack
   categories are concentrated in specific groups, and the rarest categories are the
   ones that lose the most rows. A deduplication rule that keeps the first occurrence
   silently changes the class distribution that the model will be trained on.
3. **The correct treatment is a split-time decision.** The v3 protocol requires the
   duplicate and leakage fingerprints to be computed and audited *before* partition
   assignment, so that a repeated observation cannot straddle two partitions. Deciding
   how to consolidate a group is a modelling decision that has to be taken on the
   training partition and recorded in the split manifest.
4. **The evidence must stay inspectable.** Until a split exists, the raw rows are the
   only evidence available; an automatic delete would destroy the ability to quantify
   the effect of the decision later.

For the same reason this report contains no deduplicated, resampled or re-labelled
derivative of the source file.

### Shape of the distribution

| Feature | skewness (sample) | excess kurtosis (sample) | reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DST_TO_SRC_IAT_MIN` | 336.205 | 117,679.261 | right-skewed |
| `DNS_TTL_ANSWER` | 331.816 | 113,033.964 | right-skewed |
| `RETRANSMITTED_IN_BYTES` | 142.786 | 22,893.650 | right-skewed |
| `IN_BYTES` | 142.287 | 22,804.421 | right-skewed |
| `NUM_PKTS_256_TO_512_BYTES` | 129.462 | 30,352.634 | right-skewed |
| `RETRANSMITTED_IN_PKTS` | 120.861 | 18,222.827 | right-skewed |
| `DST_TO_SRC_IAT_AVG` | 114.820 | 26,564.566 | right-skewed |
| `DST_TO_SRC_IAT_STDDEV` | 52.195 | 6,607.932 | right-skewed |

The dominant pattern is a zero-heavy, strongly right-skewed distribution: most flows
carry no payload, and a small number of flows carry very large byte counts. The
consequences for modelling are:

- A linear model on raw byte counts would be dominated by a handful of large flows.
  A log1p or a training-derived robust scaling is therefore likely to be needed, but
  the transform is a train-only decision and stays `PENDING ISSUE #7`.
- Heavy tails inflate the standard deviation, so a median-based imputation baseline is
  safer than a mean-based one for the skewed byte and duration fields.
- `IN_BYTES` and `OUT_BYTES` and their packet counterparts are strongly zero-inflated.
  Whether a zero means "no payload" or "not observed" is a semantic question about the
  exporter, not something the data can answer.

### Constant and near-constant features

Constant features detected on the real data: none.
A feature is reported as constant when the sample variance is zero, and as near-constant
when the inter-quartile range collapses to zero while the extremes still differ. Both
conditions are evaluated on the observed values, not assumed from the schema.

### Outliers and transformation risk

The maximum values are orders of magnitude above the 95th percentile for the byte,
packet and duration fields, which is the quantitative form of the heavy-tail finding
above. The baseline contract does not clip or winsorise: any clipping bound is a
training-derived decision that has to be justified on validation data and recorded with
the affected row counts, and it is not part of this EDA.

## 7. Leakage-safe EDA boundary

Issue #6 and Issue #7 reference each other: the EDA needs to know which data may be
used for design decisions, and the split protocol needs the EDA findings to define the
handling policy. This run resolves that ordering **without** assuming a split that does
not exist.

### Split status

| Item | Status |
|---|---|
| Verified train/validation/test split | PENDING ISSUE #7 |
| Expected split manifest path | `data/processed/nf_unsw_nb15_v3_split_manifest.json` |
| Leakage audit on real partitions | NOT VERIFIED |
| Train-only fitted preprocessing artifact | NOT VERIFIED |

No verified train/validation/test split manifest exists. Train-dependent analysis must not be performed and no split may be created to bypass Issue #7.

### Permitted in this run

- Full-dataset source profiling of the verified population.
- Data quality audits that do not modify the source bytes.
- Descriptive label and attack-category distributions.
- Clearly labelled exploratory visualisations.

### Not permitted in this run

- Selecting final ML features with held-out or test labels.
- Fitting imputers, encoders, scalers or selectors on the full dataset.
- Choosing thresholds or hyper-parameters with test information.
- Claiming that cross-split leakage has been verified.
- Creating an undocumented random split to bypass Issue #7.
- Automatic de-duplication or label-dependent row filtering.

### Consequence for the findings

Every observation in this report is a property of the source population. It is a valid
input for a design discussion, but it is **not** a train-only decision. Accordingly:

- No feature is selected, dropped or ranked by this report.
- No imputer, encoder, scaler, selector, resampler or threshold is fitted.
- No claim is made that cross-split leakage has been checked.
- No undocumented random split was created to work around the missing split.
- No row was removed on the basis of its label or of its duplicate status.

All train-dependent recommendations are therefore marked `PENDING ISSUE #7`.

| Check | Inherited | Recomputed by this run | Agreement |

| Rows | 2,365,424 | 2,365,424 | MATCH |

The inherited report uses a blake2b digest over the raw CSV text; this run uses a
vectorised `pandas.util.hash_pandas_object` fingerprint over the parsed values. Both
define the same row-equivalence relation, so the counts are expected to be identical. A
disagreement would mean that the publisher's formatting is not uniform across rows and
would have to be investigated before the counts could be used.

## 9. Limitations

- **Sampling.** Shape statistics (skewness, kurtosis) and every figure come from a
  reservoir sample of 200,000 rows (requested
  200,000), seed 42, method:
  reservoir sampling (Algorithm L) over the parsed population. Counts, means, extremes, exact population quantiles and
  complete-case correlations are computed over all 2,365,424 rows.
- **Float aggregation order.** Means and standard deviations are accumulated per
  streaming chunk, so the last decimal digits depend on the chunk size. The committed
  run uses the default chunk size of 100,000 rows; counts and quantiles are unaffected.
- **Provenance.** The SHA-256 pin is project-computed from the official UQRDM bytes, not
  published by the dataset authors.
- **Time coverage.** The capture window is a few weeks of 2015 traffic and does not
  support claims about contemporary networks.
- **Feature semantics.** The published feature dictionary does not expose the producer
  arithmetic, so the zero-duration / non-finite rate relation stays an observation.
- **No split, no fitted preprocessing, no model.** `ML_READY` stays `BLOCKED`; the
  duplicate handling policy and the imputation policy remain
  `PENDING ISSUE #7` and Issue #8.
- **Privacy.** No raw IP address, port pair or individual flow is exported by this
  analysis. Only aggregates and a seeded sample held in memory are used, and the sample
  contains no identifier column.
